description: Toy Box Friends G2-13 (grade 2): retell a story in order with first, next, then, last (beginning, middle, end) on the Story Stairs, and use one clue at a time to explain why a character acts.

youtube.title: First, Next, Then, Last! Story Order for Kids | Grade 2 Reading | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Four story cards land in a jumble, and Robo reads them in a silly order. Cat says: that can't be right! We watch Turtle's Windy Kite Day, an original story, then put the cards on the Story Stairs: first, next, then, last (beginning, middle and end). Cat the Why Detective uses her magnifier to find the clue for each why question: why Turtle flew his kite, why he asked Squirrel for help, and why he shared his apple. Then Robo makes a sandwich in the wrong order, and we finish with a what-comes-next challenge and a quiz.

For second graders (CCSS RL.2.1, RL.2.3, RL.2.5: retell events in order, explain why characters act).

Try at home: retell a favourite story on four fingers, first, next, then, last. Then say one why with because and the clue. Fly kites only in open spaces, away from trees and power lines, with a grown-up.

objects.text: Add frosting when they are cool.

do.text: First, Next, Then, Last
Whoa! The story cards flew off the shelf. Let me read them.
Turtle says thank you to Squirrel.
Then Turtle's kite gets stuck.
Then Turtle takes out his kite. Then he flies it.
Saying thank you before anyone helped? That can't be the right order.
A story only makes sense when things happen in order.
Let's build the Story Stairs. One step for each part of the story.
First.
Next.
Then.
Last.
These are signal words. They tell us the order things happen.
signal words
You can't skip to the top. Each step needs the one below it.
first, next, then, last
The first part of a story is the beginning.
Next and then are the middle.
And last is the end.
Beginning, middle, end. Now let's watch the real story, in order.
Turtle's Windy Kite Day
First, Turtle sees leaves blowing past his house.
What a windy day! Perfect for flying my kite.
What do you think happens next?
Next, Turtle walks slowly up the hill and flies his kite high.
The string pulls tight!
Wheee! Look how high it flies!
Remember, fly kites in open spaces, away from trees and power lines.
Fly kites with a grown-up, in open spaces
What happens next?
Then, a big gust pushes the kite into a tall tree. It is stuck!
Oh no. My legs are short, and my shell is heavy. I can't climb.
How does Turtle feel now? Worried.
worried
What happens last?
Squirrel! You are a good climber. Can you help me, please?
Fun fact! Squirrels can climb down head first. They turn their back feet around.
Thank you, Squirrel! Please share my apple slices.
Last, Turtle says thank you and shares his apple. The end!
Now, which card goes first?
Which card goes first?
First, Turtle sees the leaves and takes out his kite.
Next, he walks up the hill and flies it high.
Then... Turtle says thank you!
Not yet! Nobody has helped him. The kite must get stuck first.
Then the kite gets stuck. Last, Squirrel helps, and Turtle says thank you.
Let's retell the whole story, using the signal words.
first, next, then, last
First, Turtle sees the windy leaves and takes out his kite.
Next, he flies it high on the hill.
Then, a gust blows it into a tree.
Last, Squirrel helps, and Turtle shares his apple.
First is the beginning. Next and then are the middle. Last is the end.
I'm the Why Detective. Why did Turtle fly his kite today?
Clue: the leaves are blowing. It was windy, and kites need wind to fly.
because it was windy
Fun fact! Moving air pushes up on a kite and lifts it.
Why did Turtle ask Squirrel for help?
Because Turtle can't climb trees. His legs are short. Squirrel is a good climber.
Why did Turtle share his apple?
To say thank you. He felt thankful, so he shared.
apple shared = thank you
Turtle felt excited at the beginning, worried in the middle, and thankful at the end.
When you answer why, say because, and name the clue.
because + the clue
Clue found, case closed!
First step!
Next step!
Then the top!
Last is where the story stops!
First!
Next!
Then!
Last!
Order matters in real life too. I'll make a sandwich!
Top slice first... then the filling on top!
Where is the bottom slice? Each step needs the one before it.
First, wash your hands.
1. Wash your hands
Next, take two slices of bread.
2. Two slices of bread
Then, put the filling on one slice.
3. Filling on one slice
Last, put the other slice on top.
4. The other slice on top
A real sandwich! The right order makes it work.
Challenge time! Cupcakes. Here are three steps. What comes last?
Mix the batter. Pour it into cups. A grown-up bakes them.
What comes last?
Add the frosting, once they are cool!
Frosting on a hot cupcake would melt. The order matters!
Next, Dog's bath. These cards are jumbled.
I know! Dry Dog with a towel first.
But why would that not work?
Dog isn't wet yet! You dry him after the bath.
First, get Dog wet. Next, rub in the soap.
Then, rinse off the bubbles. Last, dry him with a towel.
After the bath, Dog shakes. Why did Dog shake?
He was wet. The clue is the water drops flying off him.
Quiz time! What happened first in Turtle's story?
He saw the windy leaves and took out his kite.
What happened right after the kite got stuck?
Turtle asked Squirrel for help, and Squirrel climbed up.
Why did Turtle ask Squirrel for help?
Because Squirrel can climb, and Turtle can't.
How did Turtle feel in the middle?
Worried!
worried
Which word comes after next? First, then or last?
Then!
Let's remember. Stories go first, next, then, last. Beginning, middle, end.
And clues tell us why. Say because, and name the clue.
Try it at home! Retell a story on four fingers: first, next, then, last.
first, next, then, last
Or fold a paper into four boxes, and draw your day in order.
Bye, friends! See you next time!
